rows.observation: CFTC launched ANPRM for Regulation CTX (Crypto Asset Transactions) and Regulation CAM (Crypto Asset Markets) Oct 5; creates new Crypto Asset Market DCM subcategory for leveraged/margined retail crypto; requires FCM intermediation, DCO clearing, actual delivery test; 60-day comment period
research: "finding": "The CFTC published an Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking (ANPRM) on October 5, 2026, titled 'Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets' (RIN 3038-AF80). The ANPRM proposes Regulation CTX to define when retail crypto asset transactions (CTXs) fall under CEA Section 2(c)(2)(D) and Regulation CAM to create a new 'crypto asset market' (CAM) subcategory of designated contract market (DCM) registration for venues offering leveraged, margined, or financed retail crypto transactions. The framework would require CTXs to be intermediated by futures commission merchants (FCMs) and cleared through derivatives clearing organizations (DCOs), with an 'actual delivery' exception for transfers of crypto assets to customer-controlled wallets within 28 days. A 60-day comment period runs from Federal Register publication.",

"evidence": "Multiple sources confirm the CFTC released the ANPRM on October 5, 2026 (Release 9307-26, RIN 3038-AF80). The ANPRM covers Regulation CTX (defining CTXs under CEA §2(c)(2)(D)) and Regulation CAM (creating a CAM subcategory of DCM). It requires FCM intermediation and DCO clearing for all CTXs, with leverage only through eligible providers under CAM rulebook arrangements. The 'actual delivery' test is based on customer possession/control (e.g., private keys) within 28 days per §2(c)(2)(D)(ii). Comments are due 60 days after Federal Register publication. The ANPRM is a preliminary step, not a final rule.",
"sources": [
"CFTC Seeks Public Comment on Advanced Notice of Proposed Rulemaking Relating to Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions and Regulation Crypto Asset Markets | CFTC",
"CFTC Previews Regulation CTX and CAM: A Federal Charter for Crypto Exchanges, With Leverage as the Trigger | Fenwick",
"CFTC Launches Crypto Market Structure Rulemaking as SEC Advances Its Own Digital Asset Framework | Baker Botts",
"A New Era in Digital Assets: CFTC Announces ANPRM For Regulation CTX and Regulation CAM | Steptoe",
"CFTC Seeks Input on Crypto Asset Regulatory Framework",
"Regulation CTX would route a leverage offer onto a DCM — The Industry Spread",
"CFTC ANPRM: crypto venue rules are not live yet",
"CFTC Issues Advance Notice Of Proposed Rulemaking On Regulation Crypto Asset Transactions And Regulation Crypto Asset Markets - Commodities/Derivatives/Stock Exchanges - United States"

"context": "The ANPRM follows the Senate's failure to pass the CLARITY Act (September 15, 2026) and the SEC's proposed Regulation Crypto Assets (August 2026). It represents the CFTC's first comprehensive rulemaking effort for crypto markets under existing CEA authority, moving beyond 'regulation by enforcement.' The framework is optional — exchanges can choose state money-transmission licensing for spot-only trading, but offering leverage/margin triggers CFTC jurisdiction. The ANPRM was submitted to OIRA on September 17, 2026, and approved by the Commission on October 5, 2026.",

"uncertainty": "The observation states 'Oct 5' without a year; research confirms October 5, 2026. The 60-day comment period start date depends on Federal Register publication, which had not occurred as of early October 2026. The ANPRM is an advance notice, not a proposed or final rule — binding requirements would require subsequent rulemaking. The actual delivery test for crypto (private key possession, governance/staking rights) is the CFTC's preliminary view and subject to comment. The scope of 'covered offer' (whether a single margin clause brings all account transactions under CFTC jurisdiction) is also preliminary.",
"status": "supported"

rows.observation: ESMA MiCA stablecoin crackdown Oct 8: 3-month wind-down deadline Jan 8, 2027 for non-compliant ARTs/EMTs (USDT, PYUSD named); CASPs must not provide services; only narrow exit services permitted; no grandfathering; USDT $184B market cap still unauthorized in EU
research: "finding": "On 8 October 2026, ESMA published opinion ESMA75-113276571-1742 directing national competent authorities (NCAs) to require MiCA-authorised crypto-asset service providers (CASPs) to cease providing services related to non-MiCA-compliant asset-referenced tokens (ARTs) and e-money tokens (EMTs) — i.e., stablecoins that lack EU authorisation under MiCA Titles III/IV. CASPs must immediately block new EU-client acquisitions and limit existing services to a strictly supervised wind-down of legacy positions. NCAs should ensure remediation of remaining customer holdings as soon as possible and no later than three months after publication (8 January 2027). During the wind-down, only residual services such as liquidation, conversion, withdrawal, transfer, and safekeeping of existing holdings are permitted; new purchases, promotion, trading, active distribution, and continued market availability are prohibited. The opinion does not name specific tokens, but Tether’s USDT (market cap ~$184 billion) and PayPal USD (PYUSD) are widely identified as the largest unauthorised stablecoins affected. Private ownership and self-custody are not restricted; the measures apply only to services provided by MiCA-licensed firms. Enforcement timing and exact cut-off dates are left to individual NCAs, which may impose earlier deadlines within the three-month outer limit.",

"evidence": "Multiple authoritative sources (ESMA press releases, CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, CryptoPotato, EU AlphaPilot, Finobird, etc.) consistently report the 8 October 2026 ESMA opinion (ESMA75-113276571-1742) setting a three-month wind-down period ending 8 January 2027 for non-MiCA-compliant ARTs/EMTs. The opinion covers the full range of MiCA Title V services (trading, exchange, order execution, custody, transfers, advice, portfolio management). It explicitly rejects investor warnings as sufficient and brings custody/transfers into scope, unlike the January 2025 guidance. USDT (~$184 B) and PYUSD are repeatedly cited as the most prominent unauthorised tokens. Sources confirm no grandfathering, only narrow exit services, and that enforcement is delegated to NCAs.",

"context": "MiCA’s stablecoin rules (Titles III and IV) became applicable on 30 June 2024, requiring issuers of asset-referenced and e-money tokens offered to EU users to obtain authorisation and meet reserve, redemption, governance, and disclosure requirements. The full MiCA regime for CASPs took effect 1 July 2026, ending the transitional period. Tether has not sought MiCA authorisation for USDT, citing reserve-composition rules (e.g., 60% of reserves in EU bank deposits). Several platforms (Binance, Coinbase, Kraken, OKX) had already restricted USDT/PYUSD for EU users ahead of the ESMA opinion. The 8 October 2026 opinion is ESMA’s supervisory convergence tool under Article 29 of the ESMA Regulation, addressed to NCAs to ensure consistent enforcement across member states.",

"uncertainty": "The opinion does not publish an exhaustive list of non-compliant tokens; identification of specific ARTs/EMTs as non-compliant is left to NCAs and CASPs based on authorisation status. Exact wind-down cut-off dates may vary by NCA and platform (some may act before 8 January 2027). The research does not confirm whether Tether or PayPal will pursue MiCA authorisation before the deadline. Enforcement actions by individual NCAs (e.g., BaFin, AMF) have not yet been published as of the research date.",
"status": "supported"
